questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Regional Connectivity Scheme - Modified UDAN, approved by the Union Cabinet on 25 March 2026:
1. It has an outlay of Rs 28,840 crore over ten years, FY2026-27 to FY2035-36.
2. It seeks to develop 200 new airports from unserved airstrips and 100 helipads.
3. UDAN stands for 'Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik' and is run by the Ministry of Civil Aviation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The numbers in statement 2 are swapped: the scheme includes 100 new airports from unserved airstrips and 200 helipads. The earlier UDAN scheme had an outlay of Rs 4,500 crore, so the new ten-year commitment is far larger. UDAN is the Ministry of Civil Aviation's regional connectivity programme.

questions.q: The Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojna (BHAVYA), approved by the Union Cabinet on 18 March 2026, is a central sector scheme to:
o: provide production-linked incentives to 100 large manufacturing companies over six years
set up 100 semiconductor fabrication units with an outlay of Rs 33,660 crore
provide interest subvention on working-capital loans to 100 MSME clusters
develop 100 investment-ready plug-and-play industrial parks, with an outlay of Rs 33,660 crore over six years
questions.e: BHAVYA picks projects in challenge mode and gives central support of up to Rs 1 crore per acre. It is implemented under the National Industrial Corridor Development Programme by NICDC under DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry. It is an industrial-infrastructure scheme, not a production-linked incentive or a credit-guarantee scheme.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Small Hydro Power (SHP) Development Scheme approved on 18 March 2026:
1. It covers FY2026-27 to FY2030-31 with an outlay of about Rs 2,585 crore.
2. It targets about 15,000 MW from projects of 1 MW to 25 MW.
3. Small hydro projects up to 25 MW fall under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The target is about 1,500 MW, not 15,000 MW; the scheme is expected to attract about Rs 15,000 crore of investment, which may be the source of the confusion. Projects up to 25 MW are classed as small hydro and are handled by MNRE, whereas larger hydro projects fall under the Ministry of Power.

questions.q:
Statement-I: On 18 March 2026 the Union Cabinet approved reimbursement of Rs 1,718 crore to the Cotton Corporation of India for MSP operations in the 2023-24 cotton season.
Statement-II: The Cotton Corporation of India buys cotton at MSP when market prices fall below the support price.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: In 2023-24 cotton prices fell below MSP, so CCI bought about 33 lakh bales from 7.25 lakh farmers at the support price and incurred losses. The reimbursement makes good these losses and took total support to Rs 11,712 crore. Statement-II explains why the Centre has to reimburse CCI.

questions.q: Press Note 2 of 2026, issued by DPIIT on 15 March 2026, relaxed FDI rules for investors from countries sharing a land border with India by:
o: permitting Pakistani citizens and entities to invest through the automatic route in all sectors except defence
removing the requirement that the beneficial owner be situated in such a country and adopting the PMLA definition of beneficial ownership (more than 10%)
scrapping the government approval requirement for every investment from land-border countries
lowering the beneficial-ownership threshold to 5% so that more investors fall under the approval route
questions.e: The change eases the Press Note 3 (2020) regime, which mainly affected China, by narrowing the beneficial-ownership test. It does not open the automatic route to all such investors, and Pakistani citizens and entities still need government approval and are barred from sectors such as defence and atomic energy.

questions.q:
With reference to RoDTEP, consider the following statements:
1. On 23 March 2026 the government fully restored RoDTEP benefits by removing the 50% cap on remission rates introduced in February 2026.
2. RoDTEP was launched in 2021, replacing the MEIS.
3. RoDTEP replaced the Duty Drawback scheme.
4. The restoration was justified by logistics disruption from the West Asia conflict.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: RoDTEP (Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products) refunds embedded taxes and duties not otherwise rebated and replaced MEIS, not the Duty Drawback scheme, which continues. The government cited West Asia disruption to logistics when it removed the temporary 50% cap.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about RBI measures in March 2026:
1. RBI raised the maximum dividend payout ratio to 75% of profit after tax from 50% for eligible banks.
2. A draft framework of 6 March proposes compensating a customer 85% of net loss or Rs 25,000, whichever is lower, for fraudulent transactions up to Rs 50,000, available once in a lifetime.
3. Under the dividend directions, extraordinary income and Level 3 unrealised gains are excluded from profit after tax.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The payout ceiling was raised from 40%, not 50%, to 75% on 10 March 2026. The draft customer-liability framework is a limited, once-in-a-lifetime compensation, with banks paying within five calendar days and seeking quarterly reimbursement from the RBI. Excluding extraordinary income prevents one-off gains from inflating dividends.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about India's flexible inflation target, retained in March 2026, is NOT correct?
o: The target applies for the period 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031
The target of 4% with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2% is fixed by the RBI Monetary Policy Committee on its own
The framework of flexible inflation targeting was adopted in 2016
The target of 4% is accompanied by a tolerance band of plus or minus 2%
questions.e: Under Section 45ZA of the RBI Act, 1934 the Central Government, in consultation with the RBI, notifies the inflation target every five years. It retained 4% (plus or minus 2%) for 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031, the second extension since March 2021. The MPC's job is to meet the target, not to set it.

questions.q: As per RBI data for Q3 2025-26 (October-December 2025), India's current account deficit was:
questions.e: The Q3 deficit widened from USD 11.3 billion (1.1% of GDP) a year earlier. The USD 14.1 billion (1.5%) figure belongs to Q2 2025-26, while USD 24.4 billion is the fall in forex reserves in Q3, not the deficit. The current account deficit measures the net shortfall on trade, services, income and transfers.

questions.q:
With reference to the Hurun Global Rich List 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It counted 308 billionaires in India.
2. India ranked third globally, after the United States and China.
3. Mumbai, with 95 billionaires, led Indian cities.
4. The list is published by Forbes.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Hurun Global Rich List is published by the Hurun Research Institute, not Forbes (which publishes its own Billionaires list). India counted 308 billionaires, third behind the US and China, and Mumbai led its cities with 95.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding India's use of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 in March 2026:
1. It was invoked to direct refiners to maximise LPG production and prioritise domestic households over industry and petrochemicals.
2. Section 3 of the Act empowers the Centre to regulate the production, supply and distribution of essential commodities.
3. Only State Governments may exercise the powers under Section 3.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The step responded to West Asia supply disruption, as India imports about 60% of its LPG demand. Section 3 vests the regulatory power in the Central Government, which can also delegate it to States, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q: The Ministry of Heavy Industries revised the PM E-DRIVE scheme in March 2026. Which one of the following correctly states the revised subsidy periods?
o: Electric two-wheelers until 31 July 2026 and electric three-wheelers (rickshaws and carts) until 31 March 2028
Electric two-wheelers until 31 March 2028 and electric three-wheelers until 31 July 2026
Both electric two-wheelers and three-wheelers until 31 March 2028
Both electric two-wheelers and three-wheelers until 31 July 2026
questions.e: The revision shortens the window for two-wheelers, the high-volume segment, while giving three-wheelers a much longer runway. The scheme's Rs 10,900 crore outlay was approved in October 2024 and includes 72,300 public fast chargers.

questions.q: The Mineral (Auction) Second Amendment Rules, 2026, notified by the Ministry of Mines on 30 March 2026:
o: remove the auction premium on all critical minerals, including graphite, phosphate and potash, regardless of their share of block value
remove the auction premium on critical minerals, except graphite, phosphate and potash, that form less than 10% of block value
impose a higher auction premium on critical minerals that form more than 10% of block value
transfer the regulation of mineral auctions from the Ministry of Mines to the Indian Bureau of Mines
questions.e: The relaxation is meant to make blocks with minor critical-mineral content more attractive to bidders. Graphite, phosphate and potash are excluded from the relief. A separate set of amendments requires States to decide mineral-inclusion applications within 60 days.

questions.q: On 23 March 2026 the SEBI Board adopted High-Level Committee recommendations on conflict of interest. Which one of the following is among them?
o: Only the Chairman is to be treated as an 'insider', while Whole-Time Members may hold listed equity freely
The Chairman and Whole-Time Members may keep existing equity holdings provided they disclose them once a year
The Chairman and Whole-Time Members are to be treated as 'insiders', with equity holdings liquidated, frozen or sold on joining
The Chairman and Whole-Time Members are barred from investing in mutual funds and every other regulated product
questions.e: The Board also capped investment in any one intermediary's products at 25% of the official's financial portfolio, with prospective limits extending to spouses and dependent family members and periodic disclosures. SEBI was set up under the SEBI Act, 1992 to regulate the securities market.

questions.q: Under the National Highways Fee (Second Amendment) Rules, effective 17 March 2026, a vehicle recorded crossing an electronic toll point without paying the user fee is liable to a penalty of:
o: the same amount as the toll
questions.e: The Rules define an 'unpaid user fee' and set a penalty of twice the toll. Only the original fee is payable if it is paid within 72 hours of the e-notice, and after 15 days the dues are recorded in the VAHAN database and restrictions may follow. The incentive is to push users to pay promptly.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Union Government's fiscal measures in March 2026:
1. The Rajya Sabha approved the second batch of Supplementary Demands for Grants for 2025-26.
2. The Finance Minister introduced a Rs 1 lakh crore Economic Stabilisation Fund as a buffer against global shocks.
3. Supplementary grants are presented to Parliament under Article 115 of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Money votes are the Lok Sabha's preserve: it approved the second batch of Supplementary Demands for Grants, not the Rajya Sabha. Article 115 covers supplementary, additional and excess grants. The government said the 2025-26 revised fiscal deficit target of 4.4% of GDP was unchanged.

questions.q: Which one of the following correctly describes the modified Mutual Credit Guarantee Scheme for MSMEs (MCGS-MSME)?
o: The NCGTC guarantees 60% of loans up to Rs 100 crore, the minimum machinery-and-equipment share of project cost falls from 75% to 60%, and service-sector MSMEs become eligible
CGTMSE guarantees 60% of loans up to Rs 100 crore, and the minimum machinery-and-equipment share rises from 60% to 75%
The NCGTC guarantees 100% of loans up to Rs 10 crore, and only manufacturing MSMEs remain eligible
The NCGTC guarantees 60% of loans up to Rs 100 crore, but service-sector MSMEs are excluded and the machinery share rises to 75%
questions.e: The modification follows the Union Budget 2025-26 announcement. The guarantee lasts 10 years and the scheme covers loans sanctioned over four years or until Rs 7 lakh crore of cumulative guarantees, whichever is earlier. NCGTC is the National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company, distinct from CGTMSE.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Grameen Credit Score:
1. NABARD directed banks to use it as the default tool for assessing rural borrowers.
2. It is a score on a 300-900 scale developed by credit information companies.
3. It was announced in the Union Budget 2025-26.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: It was the Department of Financial Services, not NABARD, that directed banks to use the score, especially for first-time rural borrowers. Phase I draws on data such as Kisan Credit Cards, SVAMITVA records, priority sector loans and tractor loans. Statement 3 is correct: the score was announced in Budget 2025-26.

questions.q:
Consider the following food-safety reforms approved in March 2026:
1. FSSAI licences and registrations are given perpetual validity.
2. From 1 April 2026 the registration turnover threshold rises from Rs 12 lakh to Rs 1.5 crore.
3. Street vendors registered under the Street Vendors Act, 2014 are deemed registered under FSSAI.
4. FSSAI functions under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The reforms were approved by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, under which FSSAI functions as the regulator under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. Statement 4 is therefore wrong. Licensing at the State level covers businesses up to Rs 50 crore turnover.

questions.q:
A Parliamentary panel recommended IPOs for profitable Regional Rural Banks in March 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. RRBs earned a consolidated net profit of Rs 7,720 crore in the first nine months of FY2025-26.
2. Under the RRB structure, the Centre holds 35%, the sponsor bank 50% and the State government 15%.
3. Gross NPAs of RRBs stood at a 13-year low of 5.4%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: RRB ownership is Centre 50%, sponsor bank 35% and State government 15%, so statement 2 swaps the first two. The One State-One RRB policy has cut the number of RRBs from a peak of 196 to 28. Profitability and low NPAs are the case the panel made for listing.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding NMDC:
1. It became the first mining company in India to produce 50 million tonnes of iron ore in a single financial year.
2. It operates India's only mechanised diamond mine, at Panna in Madhya Pradesh.
3. It is a Maharatna public sector enterprise under the Ministry of Mines.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: NMDC (incorporated 1958) is a Navratna CPSE under the Ministry of Steel, not a Maharatna under the Ministry of Mines, so statement 3 is wrong. The 50 million tonne milestone and the Panna diamond mine are correct.

questions.q: The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy introduced List-III of the Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM). It covers:
o: solar ingots and wafers, effective 1 June 2028
questions.e: List-III follows the ALMM lists for solar modules and cells and moves the domestic-sourcing requirement further upstream in the solar value chain. The order of the lists mirrors the manufacturing sequence from wafers to cells to modules.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the RELIEF scheme (Resilience & Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation):
1. It was launched by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry with an outlay of Rs 497 crore.
2. It offers credit-insurance support through new ECGC cover for 16 March to 15 June 2026 for exports to 10 West Asian countries.
3. It was launched by the Ministry of Finance for all exporters worldwide.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: RELIEF is aimed at exporters hit by the West Asia crisis, with up to Rs 50 lakh of cover per MSME exporter without prior insurance. ECGC provides export credit insurance. It is a Commerce Ministry scheme confined to West Asian destinations, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding PRARAMBH 2026:
1. It is a nationwide awareness campaign on the Income Tax Act, 2025, launched by the Finance Minister.
2. The Income Tax Act, 2025 takes effect from 1 April 2026.
3. 'Kar Saathi' is a physical helpline staffed by tax officers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: 'Kar Saathi' is an AI chatbot, not a staffed helpline. The campaign also includes Income Tax Website 2.0, brochures in 10 regional languages plus English and Hindi, and a MyGov quiz. The Income Tax Act, 2025 replaces the Income-tax Act, 1961.

questions.q: The Controller General of Accounts reported that the Centre's fiscal deficit reached Rs 12.52 trillion by the end of February 2026. This was what share of the full-year 2025-26 target (4.4% of GDP)?
questions.e: The Rs 12.52 trillion figure is 80.4% of the full-year target of Rs 15.58 trillion. A year earlier the comparable ratio was higher at 85.8%, so the deficit had used up a smaller share of its target than a year before. The CGA functions under the Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance.
